notes:
Passed on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked); no hardware was attached, the hardware backend was never opened, and no upstream module was imported or run. The package is model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json has reviewed_by null, and the loader refuses its R2 hardware backend until a human signs it. The last gate run (python3 -m mhs.driver check ... --backend fake) passed G1-G9 with no findings and no warnings (no G4.REF_VALUE, no G4.REF_BINARY); the digest line is recorded in gate.digest. No PDF was cited. The clone stayed unmodified at a8f2409fa6924b1aed83e1224c34a0528b5cb002.

SCOPE: the package binds fish_sorter.hardware.valve_controller:ValveController, one of the card's entry symbols: the Wago/CoDeSys pneumatic valve controller of the Fish Sorter v2. Reads: draw_time_ms, expel_time_ms and function_code from the holding registers. Writes: the draw and expel timing registers, both Limit.operator_required because no text of the clone states a range; site-limits.example.json is an example-only 1-5000 ms narrowing and is operator data, not a device fact. Actions: x-cap.czbiohub-sf.set_pressure.v1, set_vacuum.v1 and idle_atmospheric.v1 write the same function codes that PickingPipette.pressure/vacuum/idle write; the input-free x-cap.czbiohub-sf.safe_pneumatics.v1 is the safe_state.achieved_by action and the stop path: the @estop writes the atmospheric-idle function code once, with no wait. estop.kind is software; the clone's text documents no independent physical e-stop, and none is claimed. The clone has no read-back that confirms the valves physically reached idle, so the driver claims only the function-code write, not sensed quiescence.

NOT COVERED: the Zaber x/y/p pipette stage and the PickingPipette.draw/expel timed pulses. ZaberController has no stop, abort, halt or disable method (zaber_controller.py:11-176) and move_arm blocks with timeout=60 (zaber_controller.py:126-159); the clone cannot cancel a move in flight. PickingPipette.disconnect is not an e-stop: it commands clearance, homes x/y and swings the pipette before writing idle (picking_pipette.py:81-94). The timed draw/expel helpers only poll the function register and never abort (picking_pipette.py:213-229); exposing them would claim a stop path the native API cannot enforce. This is also why the package is scoped to the valve-controller entry symbol rather than claiming whole-instrument coverage.

FAKE: an in-memory stand-in at the ValveController method level; its public read_register/write_register/disconnect surface matches the upstream and G7 passed. It opens no socket and is neither a recording nor an upstream simulator. Every test number in fake.py is marked '# placeholder'; the driver reads the deployed register map from native.config. The fake's immediate replies do not prove real stop timing: ValveController.write_register closes, reconnects once and retries the same write [...]

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked every Fact, both operator_required limits and the stop path against the clone at the pin (the Python code, the shipped pneumatic config, valve_test.py, and the CoDeSys program text of hardware/valve_control/FishSorterValveControl.pro read with strings: code 128 sets Vacuum := 0 and Press := 0, and each accepted code is echoed to %MW6 and cleared from %MW4) and re-ran the gate. The author's package passed but ignored every Modbus write reply although pymodbus returns an exception reply as a message (valve_test.py:88-96), so a refused idle write still gave a completed e-stop; its fake kept written codes in the function register, which its e-stop test asserted; its stop was an unconfirmed write; and a command that had passed the latch check could still write after the stop. The reviewer changed driver.py (an exception reply fails, a raised or unreadable write is unknown; every command and the safe-state action wait at most 0.5 s until the controller took the code, function register 0 and echo equal to the code, so an e-stop completes only then and otherwise fails SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held; one lock per Modbus transaction with a cancellation check before each ordinary write; a function_echo read; vacuum descriptions, safe_state and ten Facts corrected, five added), fake.py (models the controller program and exception replies, with test hooks), native.py (config validated and unwrapped before connecting, unknown options and an unopened socket refused), test_driver.py (three cases rewritten, ten added, the stock gate case unchanged) and facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate passes G1-G9 with no finding and an unchanged stable digest (sha256:48d42373d314608a6a374f0fbee07dae11a3d7cf7b84a75d4fa0e2fa81cd42ce), collect.py --strict passes with no warning, all 16 tests pass, and the author's notes describing an unchecked one-write stop with no read-back are superseded. For the human reviewer: Scope is the Wago pneumatic valve controller only; the Zaber x/y/p pipette stage is NOT COVERED (ZaberController has no stop, abort or halt, move_arm passes timeout=60 to the library, and its _connect homes every stage on open in env prod), so the instrument's motion has no MHS stop. The stop's meaning and its confirmation rest on the CoDeSys program text in a binary file that no Fact can cite: check on the real controller that the deployed program matches it (codes 8, 9, 16, 17 and 128, echo in %MW6, function register cleared to 0); the confirmation proves that the program took the idle code, not a sensed valve position. Per the program text, a draw or expel sequence started by another client (the upstream GUI) takes no new code until it ends, so an e-stop during one fails SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held and the background retry sends the idle code again; the sequence ends with both outputs off after its set time (other clients can set that register without this package's limits). The upstream's connect and disconnect write idle_atm to %MW14, which the program text does not declare, so they do not idle the valves; closing the endpoint only disconnects and leaves the valves as last commanded. Per the SOP PDF the pressure box runs at 15 psi and 25 inHg of vacuum, and no emergency stop is documented: identify the physical stop (air supply or the pressure box power switch) before a hardware run (SAFE-046). On a dead link the e-stop waits for the Modbus transaction in flight (pymodbus timeout=5, retries=3, then the upstream reconnect) and fails at its 1 s budget. Licence: LICENSE is BSD-3-Clause, pyproject.toml also declares CERN-OHL-W, and hardware-license.txt (hardware/, where the CoDeSys program sits) is CERN-OHL-W; the package copies no file of the clone.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-sonnet-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Adversarial verification of the claude-opus-5-5 review (fix) by a different model (the user chose Claude Sonnet as the different model, 2026-11-04): the verifier agreed and found no blocker or major. No blocker or major found. I re-ran collect.py --strict: 1 of 1 package passes, 0 warnings. I re-ran test_driver.py: 16 tests OK. I checked all 19 Fact citations with show_refs.py against the clone at the pin, and each cited range says what its Fact claims. Strings on the .pro binary confirm the reviewer's CoDeSys claims: code 128 runs Idle with Vacuum := 0 and Press := 0, and FuncEcho is at %MW6. The driver checks Modbus reply objects and confirms the take through the function and echo registers. It holds the latch with SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED if the idle code is not taken. It has no re-enable or reset. Both write limits are operator_required, with no invented numbers. The valves-only scope is stated openly. The task.json card in the package directory has no 'stops for both stage and valves' text, so a block would have no basis there. I did not look for the precedent the reviewer cites.
